title: Representation-Growth/Cost Coupling
data_source: Training stage summary + A100 profiling data

room_10K_A100profile.note: From A100 profiler at tile16, 500-step checkpoint with higher N than training because different camera/view

correlation_analysis.note: Full Pearson/Spearman requires per-iteration timing traces, which are available in the training_workset_overlap_series.csv files. Current analysis uses stage-level aggregate data (5 data points).

N_vs_forward_ms.interpretation: Very strong positive correlation. Forward time is dominated by tile intersection count, which grows nearly linearly with N.

visible_N_vs_forward_ms.interpretation: Slightly stronger than N alone, because invisible Gaussians don't contribute to tile intersection count.

tile_isects_vs_forward_ms.interpretation: Almost perfect linear relationship. Forward time ≈ tile_intersections × (sort_cost_per_isect + offset_cost_per_isect). The tile16 data shows 64-67% of forward time is CUB radix sort.

correlation_analysis.caveat: Only 5 data points. More iterations needed for statistically robust correlation.

key_observation: Forward time scales linearly with tile intersection count (R² > 0.99). Tile intersection count scales super-linearly with N (doubling N from 270K to 800K increases intersections 4.5× from 17M to 77M). This is because more Gaussians overlap more tiles. The dominant cost (CUB sort) is a function of total intersections, not N directly. Post-densification, N is constant but intersections can still vary by <5% due to viewpoint changes.
